name: PowerView - Get-DomainUser (User Enumeration)
description: Queries AD for detailed user object attributes using PowerView. Can query any user, all users, or filter by property. Returns rich attribute set including UAC flags, logon history, SPN, group membership context, and password metadata. Foundation of PowerView-based user enumeration.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== KEY USER ATTRIBUTES TO LOOK FOR ===
  pwdlastset         → when was password last changed? Old dates = stale/weak passwords
  lastlogon          → when did user last log in? Never = service account or unused
  badpwdcount        → failed login attempts - close to threshold = careful with spraying
  useraccountcontrol → UAC flags (see below)
  memberof           → direct group memberships (use -Recurse for full nesting)
  serviceprincipalname → set = Kerberoastable
  description        → often contains passwords set by lazy admins!
  admincount         → 1 = was/is a privileged account (SDProp protected)

=== UAC FLAG VALUES TO WATCH ===
  512   = NORMAL_ACCOUNT
  514   = ACCOUNTDISABLE
  528   = LOCKOUT
  544   = PASSWD_NOTREQD
  4096  = WORKSTATION_TRUST_ACCOUNT (machine account)
  66048 = DONT_EXPIRE_PASSWD + NORMAL (service accounts often have this)
  4194304 = DONT_REQ_PREAUTH → AS-REP Roastable!
  Use: Convert-UACValue -Value <int> from PowerView to decode

=== USEFUL FILTERS ===
  All users:
    Get-DomainUser | select samaccountname,description,pwdlastset,memberof
  Find description field passwords:
    Get-DomainUser | select samaccountname,description | ? {$_.description -ne $null}
  AS-REP roastable:
    Get-DomainUser -UACFilter DONT_REQ_PREAUTH | select samaccountname
  Kerberoastable:
    Get-DomainUser -SPN | select samaccountname,serviceprincipalname
  Disabled accounts:
    Get-DomainUser -UACFilter NOT_ACCOUNTDISABLE  (flip: active accounts only)

=== QUERY CROSS-DOMAIN ===
  Get-DomainUser -Domain LOGISTICS.INLANEFREIGHT.LOCAL | select samaccountname Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 21 (Active Directory Introduction and Enumeration).

defense.why_it_works: In Active Directory the default security descriptor grants the built-in 'Authenticated Users' group read access to nearly every directory object (users, groups, computers, GPOs, trusts) and their attributes. So any valid domain account - however low-privileged - can enumerate the whole directory over LDAP/SAMR without hitting access-denied, which is why this returns data without needing admin. PowerView wraps the same LDAP reads with convenient filtering (admincount, SPN, description) any user can perform.
defense.prerequisites: Valid domain credentials (any authenticated user) and network access to a DC (LDAP 389/636).
defense.impact: A detailed user inventory revealing roasting targets, stale accounts, and embedded secrets.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1087.002] Broad/bulk LDAP queries to the DC (Event 4662 directory-service access; Microsoft Defender for Identity reconnaissance alerts); one host reading large swaths of the directory in a short window.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog EventCode=4104 (ScriptBlockText=\"*Get-DomainUser*\" OR ScriptBlockText=\"*Get-NetUser*\")
| table _time, Computer, User, ScriptBlockText
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "PowerShellCommand"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Get-DomainUser", "Get-NetUser")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
defense.prevention: AD is readable by any authenticated user by design, so prevention is limited - focus on DETECTION (Defender for Identity, LDAP/SMB anomaly monitoring), least privilege, disabling anonymous/null sessions, and REDUCING what's exposed (remove unnecessary SPNs, descriptions with secrets, over-shared folders).
defense.evasion: Use built-in tools (net, AD module, dsquery) that blend with normal admin activity; throttle and scope collection; avoid the noisiest methods (full BloodHound sweeps, RID brute) where Defender for Identity is present.
defense.misconfiguration: Active Directory's default read ACL allows any authenticated domain user to enumerate nearly the entire directory: all user accounts, groups, SPNs, computer objects, trust relationships, and many sensitive attributes. There is no built-in 'need to know' principle on LDAP reads. BloodHound, PowerView, and ldapsearch all exploit these open default ACLs to map attack paths.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# AD default permissions - authenticated users can read:
# All user objects: sAMAccountName, userPrincipalName, memberOf, servicePrincipalName
# All computer objects: DNS names, OS versions, operating system attributes
# All group memberships, GPOs, OU structure, domain trusts

# Verify with any low-priv account:
Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties *  # returns all users + attributes
Get-ADGroup -Filter * | Get-ADGroupMember  # all group memberships
defense.secure_config:
# 1. Enable AD Recycle Bin + Protected Users group
# 2. Audit and tighten ACLs on sensitive attributes:
#    msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo, adminCount, memberOf for privileged groups

# 3. Disable SMB null sessions + restrict LDAP anonymous binds (see smb/ldap cards)

# 4. Detect enumeration via volume:
# Sysmon Event 3 (network connection) from non-DC to DC on port 389/636
# Event 4661 - access to SAM objects (high-volume; baseline first)
# Microsoft Defender for Identity: 'Account Enumeration Reconnaissance' alert

# 5. Deploy Honey accounts/objects:
# Fake high-priv account (no real access) - any LDAP query for it = attacker
# BloodHound run from non-DC = detectable via DC LDAP traffic volume

# 6. Tiered administration: Tier 0 DCs, Tier 1 servers, Tier 2 workstations
#    Each tier can only query its own tier's objects

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Reads detailed user attributes with PowerView:
  Get-DomainUser   query user objects
  -Identity <user>   a specific account (omit for all users)
  -Domain <domain>   target a specific domain
Returns UAC flags, SPN, logon history, admincount, and password metadata; select the columns you need, or pipe to a description filter to hunt for creds.
